object_description: sculpturally offset school volume framing a continuous playground
design_condition: Shortening and shifting the northern wing strengthens the relationship between park and recreation area, while the offset toward the street creates a head condition and the playground extends along the building between the entrance hall and sports field.

positive.statement: The revision improves the criticized points while refining the previously convincing features of the design.

position.rationale: The elongated shifted and articulated building form is clearly visible across all projections.

positive.statement: The entrance hall has the necessary spaciousness and skillfully mediates between the different scales of adjacent exterior and interior spaces.

position.rationale: The hall is approximated at the building's lower central transition zone.

positive.statement: The simplified playground design appears more spacious while retaining possibilities for retreat and use.

position.rationale: The open strip alongside the elongated volume provides the likely playground location.

positive.statement: The functional facade expression draws on the history of the former industrial site.

position.rationale: Long ribbon-like facade bands and windowless ends are clearly visible in elevation.

positive.statement: The urban design, balanced relationship between building height and open spaces, and appropriate scale are convincing.

position.rationale: The building-to-open-space balance is represented by the elongated footprint and adjacent void.

negative.statement: The shift on the street side and the emphasis on a windowless front facade weaken the deliberate sculptural response to the different surrounding scales.

position.target: street-side shift and windowless front facade
position.rationale: The street-facing front is approximated along the southern edge with its solid end condition.

negative.statement: The jury would like a stronger emphasis on the building as an important public building.

position.rationale: Public-building identity is a whole-design judgment without one spatially isolable feature.

negative.statement: The aesthetic and maintenance longevity of the proposed photovoltaic facade still requires proof.

position.rationale: The facade system is not distinguishable from sampled points, so it receives an upper-envelope estimate.
